---
name: visio
description: How a visio site is built and deployed - the visio() plugin, the Vercel or Cloudflare build, the prerender crawl and its guards, pending links, and plugin order. Read before changing vite.config.ts, the build, the deploy, or anything the crawl has to reach.

# visio: build and deploy

`vite.config.ts` is one `visio()` call; `visio/DESIGN.md` (in `packages/` of the visio repo, `vendor/visio/` in a project) lists its options.

There is one build, and it always crawls, then writes the output of the site's deploy target. `deploy` is required: `deploy: vercel()` from `@visio/vercel`, or `deploy: cloudflare()` from `@visio/cloudflare`, with that package in the site's dependencies (`"@visio/vercel": "workspace:*"`). There is no default, and the build never guesses the target from the env. The `Router` of `src/routes.ts` tells the crawl about routes nothing links to; the pages of a dynamic route are found through links, and through the route's `announce` (the `router` skill).

- **The app root is the same in every site.** `src/app.tsx` renders the `Router` of `src/routes.ts`, and inside it, once each: `<PageTransitions router={Router} />` from `@visio/transitions` as the outlet, and, for a site with smooth scrolling, `<SmoothScroll />` from `@visio/scroll`. With Sanity, `<VisualEditing exit={...} overlay={...} />` from `@visio/sanity` goes there too, with the site's own controls for draft mode (the `sanity` skill, `references/preview.md`). WebGL is the project's own code, written for what it draws (the `frame` skill, `references/webgl.md`). The `scroll` and `transitions` skills have the rules for each.
- **With `deploy: vercel()`, the build is the Vercel deployment.** The crawl renders every static route through the built server, in order (no streamed placeholders), and `vercel()` writes `.vercel/output`: every page that is not `live` is cached by Vercel, a crawled one seeded with its HTML and any other path of a dynamic route from its first request, and so is every `prerendered()` read; one live server function answers the rest: API routes, sessions, the `live` routes (never cached), and Sanity's draft mode. `vercel/DESIGN.md` has the details.
- **With `deploy: cloudflare()`, the build is a Cloudflare Worker** in `dist/cloudflare/`, and `wrangler deploy` in the site's folder deploys it. Deploy on the Workers Paid plan: the free plan's 10 ms of CPU per request does not hold the render of a page that is not cached. In Workers Builds, set the root directory to the site's folder and the build command to `bun run build`, and keep the default deploy command (`npx wrangler deploy`) and preview command (`npx wrangler preview`). Workers Builds gives the Worker's name to the build; from a laptop, deploy with `wrangler deploy --name <worker>`. Set custom domains in the dashboard. Workers Cache keeps every page that is not `live`, and the crawled reads, in its `Render` entrypoint; the default entrypoint handles drafts, the gate, the Studio and every live path. `bun run env:push production` sets the server's variables (`SANITY_*`, `SITE_PASSWORD`) as Worker secrets and as build variables of the production branch (the `env` skill). Every branch that is not the production branch gets a Preview, which has none of production's variables or secrets: set each secret once with `wrangler preview base-config secret put NAME`, which reaches only the Previews created after it (`wrangler preview secret put NAME --name <preview>` for one that exists). The build writes the Preview's `VISIO_BYPASS_TOKEN` itself. A Version URL (`wrangler versions upload`) is not a Preview: it runs with production's settings. Only a build of the production branch is indexable: `main`, or `VISIO_PRODUCTION_BRANCH` in the build variables; a preview build with `PUBLIC_SITE_INDEXABLE=true` drops it with a warning. Wrangler must be 4.135.0 or later, and the build stops on an older one. Do not add a `wrangler.json` or a `public/_headers`: the build writes both. Tag and purge cached data of your own with `tagCache()` and `purgeCache()` from `@visio/router`, never `@vercel/functions`. `bunx wrangler dev` runs the output in workerd on your machine. To see requests only the Worker sees, such as AI crawlers, give `cloudflare({ observe: "src/observe.ts", bindings: { ANALYTICS: bindings.worker({ worker: "analytics" }) } })`: the module's default export gets `{ request, status, kind, path, env, ctx }` after each answer (`kind` is `page`, `markdown`, `robots`, `llms`, `sitemap` or `other`), reports in `ctx.waitUntil`, and cannot change the answer; with it, robots.txt, llms.txt and the sitemap run through the Worker. A Preview gets no binding, so check that `env.ANALYTICS` is there. Anything the Worker reaches on Cloudflare (another Worker, KV, R2, D1, a queue, an email sender) is a binding: `cloudflare({ bindings: { EMAIL: bindings.sendEmail({ destinationAddress: "…" }) } })`, with `bindings` from `@visio/cloudflare`, never a hand-written `wrangler.json`. A Worker cannot fetch another Worker of the same account by its URL (error 1042): bind it with `bindings.worker({ worker: "feeds" })`. In server code read a binding with `binding<SendEmail>("EMAIL")` from `@visio/cloudflare/server`, never `cloudflare:workers`, which stops the crawl. A variable or a secret is not a binding: it goes in `src/env.ts`. Bindings are production's only: `binding()` is undefined in `vite dev`, the crawl and a Preview, so a Preview sends no mail and writes no production data. Fall back there: to the other Worker's URL, declared in `src/env.ts`, or to nothing. On Cloudflare it warns once for a name with no binding; in a Preview that warning is expected. Workers Logs keeps one log per request, with the visitor's IP and location; a site that must not store IPs gives `cloudflare({ observability: { logs: { invocationLogs: false } } })`, which keeps `console.log` and `console.error`. `cloudflare/DESIGN.md` has the details.
- **`SITE_PASSWORD` puts the deployment behind a password.** Set at build time, the Vercel output gets an edge middleware, and the Cloudflare Worker a gate that runs first, which asks for it before any page, file or function is served (`@visio/gate`, `gate/DESIGN.md`); unset, nothing is added. It is the only switch: no `visio()` option, scope it to Preview in Vercel to gate previews only. The dev server is never gated. Sanity's publish hook at `/api/sanity/revalidate` passes on its own secret.
- The crawl has no option. `visio()` wires it with the server-function capture, a guard that fails the build on a page written without the content of a `<Loading>` boundary, because it never resolved or it threw (the message names the page and boundary), a guard that fails it on a page written without its route head (its `meta()` threw, or a preload it reads rejected), `robots.txt`, and the sitemap, `llms.txt` and the AI crawler rules of `robots.txt` (the `aeo` skill) when the env sets `PUBLIC_SITE_URL` and `PUBLIC_SITE_INDEXABLE=true`. Every page also answers as Markdown at `/path.md` and to `Accept: text/markdown`, on both targets. The origin and that go-ahead are read from the env by `visio()` itself, never passed as options. The crawl starts at `/`, follows every same-origin link, and fails the build on one without a page. While the nav links to pages that are not built yet, list them in `defineRoutes([...], { pending: ['/about'] })` in `src/routes.ts`, so the crawl skips them; a family of dynamic pages is a pattern (`'/work/:slug'`). The build warns for each (`ROUTE_PENDING`) and fails once its page is in the table (`PENDING_HAS_PAGE`), so remove it as the page ships. The smoke run skips them too.
- Plugin order matters, and `visio()` holds it: `images()`, `svg()`, `visio:icons`, `styling()`, `visio:aeo:dev`, `solid()`, `router()`, then the crawl. The styling compiler has to see a page file whole before the router splits it. Every site gets every part: no option turns one off, and `visio` does not export the plugins for a site to wire by hand (`visio/DESIGN.md` §Order).
- `extensions` of `visio()` takes the build part of an optional package, from that package's own call; its skill says how. Nothing else goes in it (`@visio/router` DESIGN.md, Extensions).
- `extensions: [sanity()]` from `@visio/sanity/vite` serves the Sanity Studio at `/studio` and Sanity's draft mode and publish routes under `/api/sanity`, ahead of `src/middleware.ts`, and keeps `sanity.types.d.ts` current; `sanity({ studio: { path, api } })` moves them. A route in `src/routes.ts` under a path an extension serves stops the build (`ROUTE_RESERVED`). The `sanity` skill covers the rest.
- **The icons come from `src/icons/`.** Put the artwork there: `icon.svg` (the tab), and if the designer supplies them, `icon-dark.svg` (the tab on a dark theme), `icon-ico.svg` (the drawing for `favicon.ico`, for example the mark on a tile, because the ICO has no dark variant) and `icon-touch.svg` or `.png` (the touch and app icons, with the background and padding drawn in). The build writes `favicon.ico`, the SVG favicon, `apple-touch-icon.png`, the 192 and 512 px icons and `manifest.webmanifest`, and the router links them in every page's head. Do not write icon `<link>` tags in `src/document.tsx`, and do not put those files in `public/`: both stop the build. Do not draw artwork yourself to fill a gap: padding, background and colours are the designer's decisions. A missing variant is fine, and the build prints one line about it. An `icon.svg` with its background drawn to the edge needs no touch file, and the build says nothing. The artwork must be square and have no `<text>`. `visio/DESIGN.md`, Icons, has the details.
- The route table is always `src/routes.ts`, and client env vars always carry `PUBLIC_` (`src/env.ts`); a different `envPrefix` in `vite.config.ts` stops the config.
- **In a project, never edit `vendor/visio/`.** It is a release of the visio packages, and `bun run visio:check` (in CI too) fails with `VENDOR_EDITED` on each edit. A bug or a missing feature in a package is a change in github.com/darkroomengineering/visio, then a release, then `bun run visio:update`. If you think a package needs a change, tell the user, and do not work around it in the project. `visio:update` also links each package skill as `.claude/skills/<name>`. Do not edit those links: the next update replaces them. `visio/DESIGN.md`, "Releases", has the details.
- The dev server prints the browser's uncaught errors, unhandled rejections, `console.error` and `console.warn` in its terminal, with the stack mapped to the source. `visio()` sets `server.forwardConsole` for this, and a `vite.config.ts` that turns it off stops the config. Read the terminal after you load a page, not only the HTTP status.
- **After a change to a page or a package, run `bun run smoke`.** It starts the dev server, loads every page in headless Chrome, and prints what only an open tab would show; exit 1 on any finding. `references/smoke.md` has what it checks and how to mark a finding a page causes on purpose.
